tagline: Thailand's eastern seaboard — Pattaya, nearby islands, and fresh seafood, all a short drive from Bangkok
introHtml:
Chonburi sits just east of Bangkok, a quick run down the motorway. It's the province with Bang Saen beach where people come to sit by the water, Pattaya that never sleeps, and Koh Larn, which you can boat out to and swim for the day.

Bangkok folks tend to drive over for the weekend, eat seafood by the sea, stop at Nong Mon market for khao lam and khanom jaak, then carry on to wander Sriracha or Sattahip. Whether you want a quiet break or a night out, you'll find both here.
bestTime: November–February — clear water, calm surf, and weather that isn't too hot, perfect for boating out to the islands

highlights.name: Pattaya
highlights.blurb: A beach city with sand, the Walking Street, and every kind of thing to do, going strong day and night

highlights.name: Bang Saen Beach
highlights.blurb: A beach close to Bangkok where people settle into deck chairs and eat seafood by the sea, with a beachfront road for cycling and jogging

highlights.name: Koh Larn
highlights.blurb: The island off Pattaya, a short boat ride out — clear water, white sand, good for swimming and snorkeling on a day trip

highlights.name: Nong Mon Market
highlights.blurb: An old roadside market on Sukhumvit selling khao lam, khanom jaak, Chinese sausage, and dried seafood — people stop here to shop before heading home

highlights.name: Sriracha
highlights.blurb: A seaside town with Koh Loy, a waterfront park, and a Japanese community, so there are plenty of authentic Japanese restaurants

highlights.name: Khao Sam Muk
highlights.blurb: A low hill by the sea near Bang Saen, with the Chao Mae Khao Sam Muk shrine, a troop of monkeys, and a viewpoint over the long beach

foodScene.name: Beachfront seafood
foodScene.note: Bang Saen, Sriracha, and Pattaya have seafood spots lined up along the water — prawns, shellfish, crab, and fresh fish that people drive out to eat right there

foodScene.name: Nong Mon khao lam
foodScene.note: Sticky rice roasted in bamboo tubes, the province's signature — buy it with khanom jaak at Nong Mon market to take home

foodScene.name: Hoy jor and khanom jaak
foodScene.note: Local snacks of the eastern coast, found at Nong Mon market and the souvenir shops

foodScene.name: Japanese food in Sriracha
foodScene.note: Sriracha has a Japanese community working in the industrial estates, so there are loads of genuine ramen, sushi, and izakaya spots

foodScene.name: Noodles and street food in town
foodScene.note: Around Chonburi town and Pattaya you'll find noodle soup, rice-and-curry, and roadside snacks to graze on all day

foodScene.name: Mu kratha
foodScene.note: Plenty of mu kratha (Thai BBQ hotpot) joints around the neighborhoods and dorm areas — the dinner that groups of friends and workers gather for

foodScene.name: International food in Pattaya
foodScene.note: Pattaya gets a lot of foreign visitors, so Indian, Russian, and European restaurants are scattered all over the city

foodScene.name: Seaside and in-town cafes
foodScene.note: Around Bang Saen, Sriracha, and Pattaya there are sea-view cafes and coffee shops to stop and rest at between sights

attractions.name: Pattaya Beach
attractions.blurb: The long beach in the heart of Pattaya, with water sports, restaurants, and a beachfront road that's busy day and night

attractions.name: Bang Saen Beach
attractions.blurb: A beach close to Bangkok where you sit in deck chairs and eat seafood by the sea, with a beachfront road for cycling

attractions.name: Koh Larn
attractions.blurb: The island off Pattaya — clear water and white sand, a boat ride out to swim and snorkel on a day trip

attractions.name: Pratumnak Hill (Pattaya Viewpoint)
attractions.blurb: A low hill in the middle of Pattaya, with a viewpoint over the whole of Pattaya Bay and the Pattaya City sign

attractions.name: Wat Khao Chi Chan
attractions.blurb: A giant gold line-engraved image of the Buddha carved into a large rock cliff, out in Bang Lamung district

attractions.name: Sanctuary of Truth
attractions.blurb: A carved-wood sanctuary by the sea in North Pattaya — the whole all-wood building tells stories of philosophy and belief

attractions.name: Nong Nooch Pattaya
attractions.blurb: A large botanical garden with several themed garden zones, cultural shows, and grounds to wander all day

attractions.name: Khao Sam Muk
attractions.blurb: A seaside hill near Bang Saen, with the Chao Mae Khao Sam Muk shrine, a troop of monkeys, and a beach viewpoint
